technical_assumptions.statement: Model A has a single 120-cell WIP and requires additional orientation changes before conversion.
Model A likely creates more transfer and queueing events due to a single WIP center and stronger right-to-left feed logic.
Model B retains the 120-cell WIP and adds a second 255-cell WIP area, which improves smoothing and starvation protection.
Model B improves natural flow and reduces direct transfer friction but introduces more conveyor length, greater capital cost and more maintenance points.
Corrugator OEE in stable industrial conditions typically sits in the 80-95% band; bottlenecks and starvation reduce this materially.
AMR / transfer / WIP policies can cut starvation by 60-87% and improve OEE by +6 points in comparable plants.

model_a.label: conservative / lower capex / more congestion risk

model_b.label: higher resilience / higher capex / stronger WIP control

comparative_scoring.decision_gap: Model B performs better on operational resilience and WIP protection; Model A remains attractive only if capex and space constraints dominate.

model_a: Higher queueing probability due to single WIP and orientation change
Increased load on transfer and conveyors during product mix shifts
Greater starvation risk during short interruptions
More frequent manual intervention and re-routing when throughput peaks
model_b: Higher civil and installation cost due to longer conveyors and extra WIP area
Greater maintenance burden for extended transfer network
Additional risk of route conflict and second-pass rehandling
Potentially more energy consumption if conveyors are overextended

overall_recommendation.decision_statement: Under the current evidence base, Model B is the stronger technical option for resilience, starvation control and dynamic WIP management, provided capex, maintenance burden and occupied footprint remain within the site envelope. Model A should be kept as a fallback or low-risk option only if the project is strongly constrained by capital, floor space or implementation schedule.
overall_recommendation.decision_rule: If available footprint, investment budget and maintenance team capacity are sufficient, prefer B. If budget or space is tight, A can be a lower-complexity fallback with a conscious trade-off against flow resilience.
overall_recommendation.caveat: This recommendation is not a final design decision until the actual PAIGE DWG/DXF geometry is validated in the Layout Workbench and benchmarked against real dispatch, WIP and downtime telemetry.

model_a_advantages: Simpler footprint and fewer conveyor sections
model_b_advantages: Lower probability of starvation under disturbance
More flexible routing and flow recovery
Potentially higher throughput stability on mixed SKUs
model_b_disadvantages: Longer material paths and more energy use
Potential second-pass handling and cross-traffic risk

decision_criteria_for_PAIGE: Available floor area and clear aisle requirements
Expected SKU mix and product volatility
Tolerance to WIP and starvation events
Need for future expansion without redesign
